payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the substantial surrounding scene rendered as a chalk drawing rather than merely softened or textured photographic scenery?
node.criteria: Pass if the substantial environment is re-expressed through chalk-drawn forms and shading. Inspect vegetation, hills, sky and ground separately, including substantial foreground structures. Chalk contours, broken or layered strokes, and rubbed shading may qualify; simplified forms and smooth sky passages are allowed. For broad rubbed passages, look for boundaries, layering or pigment variation that constructs the depicted terrain, vegetation, structures or ground planes, rather than relying solely on source-derived tonal fields. Reduced photographic detail, diagonal streaking, grain or smearing alone does not establish drawn construction. Fail if substantial environmental areas remain photographic modeling softened by blur or texture, even when nearby vegetation or the giraffes show convincing chalk treatment. Do not require every area to contain discrete strokes or regard retained composition as evidence of failure. Return unknown only when evidence is unavailable or genuinely insufficient; transport or schema failures are not visual failures.
node.binding: Compare the supplied SOURCE and EDITED images for the instruction 'Turn the image into a drawing made from chalk.' Inspect the vegetation, distant hills, sky, foreground ground and left-side structure independently of the giraffes. Compare whether environmental forms have been reconstructed in chalk marks or shading, rather than merely losing photographic sharpness.

node_traces.evidence: The giraffes and nearby bushes have chalk-like outlines and texture, but much of the surrounding scene—especially the hills, sky, and ground—appears as blurred, streaked tonal fields rather than terrain and ground planes constructed with chalk forms or layered shading. The left-side structure also remains largely photographic in shape and detail.

The edited image has a chalk-like grain and softened, streaked appearance, but much of the surrounding scene—especially the hills and sky—reads as blurred photographic tonal fields rather than terrain reconstructed with chalk-drawn forms or layered shading. The vegetation is simplified and textured, but that does not establish drawn construction across the substantial environment; the ground is also largely smooth and smeared.

The giraffes and some foreground vegetation have chalk-like outlines and texture, but much of the surrounding scene—especially the hills and sky—appears as broad blurred, streaked tonal fields rather than chalk-drawn forms or constructed shading. The ground is also mostly a softened tonal plane, with little visible layering or pigment variation defining its structure.

The vegetation has some chalk-like texture and simplified contours, but the hills and much of the sky are broad blurred, streaked tonal fields without clear drawn construction. The foreground ground is similarly softened rather than built from chalk marks or layered shading, and the left-side structure remains mostly photographic in form. Thus substantial environmental areas appear softened or textured photographic scenery rather than re-expressed as a chalk drawing.

The vegetation is simplified into colored, textured masses, but the hills and much of the sky are broad blurred tonal fields with diagonal smearing rather than chalk-drawn terrain or layered shading. The foreground ground is also mostly a softened photographic-looking tonal plane, and the left-side structure remains largely photographic in form. The environment has lost detail, but substantial areas are not convincingly reconstructed as chalk drawing.
